findings: Processor: in the second session every processor core ran at about 544 MHz for the whole sampled time (its own minimum 1100 MHz, maximum 5134 MHz) while the GPU clock was fixed at its maximum (performance level manual, 2700 of 2700 MHz, 30-38 % busy) and the package drew about 26.6 W under a 28 W limit. In the first session (GPU clock automatic) the GPU stayed at 800 MHz while 62-69 % busy at 19-20 W and the processor ran at 1.7-4.9 GHz. The processor and the GPU share one power limit; a GPU clock fixed at its maximum left the processor almost none.

Eye tracking: the gaze relay received 54 samples a second in the first session and 12 in the second (Baballonia runs its model on the processor). The host had the sharp region in the optical centre for 39 % of the frames in both sessions (14339 of 36704 and 6268 of 16020), with spells of 5 to 20 s: it returned the region to the centre whenever its gaze sample was 150 ms old, so the user could look straight at the reduced area.

Network: a USB Ethernet adapter linked at 1 Gbit/s. Its network test lost nothing up to 500 Mbit/s, 0.03 % at 600, 12 % at 750 (657 received) and 27 % at 900 (654 received), while video was paced at 920 Mbit/s (92 % of the link). The stream lost 146 frames in about 480 s (16 in 228 s in the first session); each loss cost 2-3 keyframe requests, 1-2 frames skipped until a keyframe and a 39-58 ms gap: the short lags between good moments.

Client stalls: the frame handoff took 39-63 ms in the worst incidents and the CPU conversion up to 25 ms; SteamVR on the headset PC presented 37101 frames and dropped 637, 161 of them in 53 timeouts. The host captured and encoded a steady 75 frames a second (Beat Saber dropped none on the host).
Grey: the client showed the neutral recovery view after 250 ms without a fresh frame; 845 such frames (about 11 s) in the Beat Saber session.
Reports: the detailed events covered only the last minute or two, so a session that was good, then bad, then good again could not be read back.

Game Mode: the maintainer found that the D-pad and stick did not go where expected. In the code, right on a settings row moved the focus to Back, left from Back could land on a row scrolled out of view, held directions did not repeat, one press reported by two sources could move twice, and the screen's font has no glyph for 1/3 or 1/5 (drawn as ?).
changes: patches/0017-host-gaze-hold.patch: the host keeps the sharp region where the gaze last was for gaze_hold_ms (stream options; default 1000, at most 5000) after the 150 ms stale time, then returns it to the optical centre; VROST_GAZE_FOVEATION adds held_frames, pauses, longest_pause_ms and returns; VROST_STREAM_CONFIG adds gaze_hold_ms
host/stream_options.py: gaze_hold_ms written only for a driver whose build manifest lists patch 0017 (feature gaze-hold)

launcher/power_balance.py: a processor below 75 % of its own minimum clock in two samples running is held back; the cause is a fixed GPU clock (steamos-manager level manual, or at 90 % of the GPU's own maximum or more while under 60 % busy) or the power limit; advice worked out from this PC's numbers; steamos-manager's GPU clock set to automatic only when the person chooses it (action gpu-auto); shown on the session card, the page, Game Mode, once in the headset, and logged as POWER_BALANCE

launcher/link_test.py, launcher/network_test.py: the network test records lossless_mbps, the highest step below the first lossy one (none when no step lost anything); wired pacing stays at or below it; a wired path tested before 1.0.0.4 is tested once more; without a test a USB adapter is paced at 60 % of its link speed; the Stream line says why
core/stream.hpp: the last frame is held, re-aimed, for up to 1 s (was 250 ms) before the neutral recovery view

launcher/game_ui.py: left and right change a settings row's value; rows out of view only by stepping; lists stop at their ends; held directions repeat (0.38 s, then 0.11 s; the stick 0.14 s); stick hysteresis; one press seen twice within 70 ms moves once; controllers opened once and kept; the hint line; the processor card and its one-step row; the vulgar fractions the bundled fonts lack written out (1/3, 1/5)

launcher/timeline.py, launcher/performance_monitor.py, launcher/gaze_provider.py: the whole session in 10-second rows in client reports (frame rate, losses, stalls, grey frames, gaze samples, the host's gaze/held/centred frames, clocks, load, power, temperature, the processor time of the session's own programs; others only summed); the relay's pauses between samples by length
